item.title: 269220 : I-71 North-South between MM 0.1 and 2.0 Between I-64/I-71 Interchange and Zorn Ave. in Jefferson County
item.description: Construction / Road Work : The I-71 widening and improvement project is a $50 million infrastructure investment to enhance safety and improve mobility along one of Louisville's most critical travel corridors. The two-year project, focused on increasing traffic capacity and safety, will enhance regional connectivity, provide reliable travel for years to come, and support economic growth. The project spans approximately two miles of interstate from the I-65/I-71 interchange near Frankfort Avenue to the I-71/Zorn Avenue interchange. Additional improvements include the construction of a multi-use path along Zorn Avenue between the I-71/Zorn Avenue interchange and Mellwood Avenue, as well as a new median treatment at the intersection of Zorn Avenue and Mellwood Avenue to enhance safety and better define traffic movements. The project also includes the demolition and reconstruction of the I-71 bridge over Beargrass Creek, along with a latex overlay on the I-71 bridge over I-64 at mile point 0.3 to extend the structure’s service life. For additional information, please visist https://transportation.ky.gov/DistrictFive/Pages/I-71-Widening---Louisville-.aspx.

item.title: 254857 : I-264 East-West between MM 21.5 and 22.9 Area of US-42 in Jefferson County
item.description: Construction / Road Work : UPDATE (March 23, 2026) – The Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) advises motorists of overnight lane and ramp closures on Interstate 264 East and West (Watterson Expressway) beginning Tuesday, March 24, as part of the $130 million widening and improvement project of I-264 and U.S. 42 (Brownsboro Road) [links-1.govdelivery.com]. Beginning Tuesday, March 24, at 8 p.m., through Wednesday, March 25, at 6 a.m.: Alternating lane closures will occur on I-264 East and West between mile markers 23 and 22 (from the I-264/I-71 split to U.S. 42/Brownsboro Road). Beginning Wednesday, March 25, at 8 p.m., through Thursday, March 26, at 6 a.m.: The I-264 East ramp to I-71 South will be closed. Motorists should continue on I-264 East, take I-71 North, then follow I-265 North to reconnect with I-71 South. Alternating lane closures will occur on I-264 East between mile markers 23 and 22 (from the I-264/I-71 split to U.S. 42/Brownsboro Road). Motorists should heed signage, use caution when traveling through the work zone, and plan ahead for travel delays. The highway improvement project is expected to be completed by the Fall of 2027. More details, including project timelines and traffic impacts [links-1.govdelivery.com], will be shared online as work progresses. Motorists are encouraged to sign up for email or text alerts [links-1.govdelivery.com] regarding weekly traffic impacts pertaining to the project.

item.title: 292980 : I-71/75 North Ramp to 12th Street/MLK Jr. Boulevard in Kenton County
item.description: Construction / Road Work : (June 5, 2026) – Interstate 71/75 ramp closures and detours in Covington are needed to safely advance construction on the Brent Spence Bridge Corridor Project, which will add interstate lanes, better access, a new companion bridge and convert the existing bridge for local travel to improve safety and increase regional highway capacity. Temporary closures and detours will now begin on Monday, June 8, and will take place in multiple phases. On Monday, June 8, the following closures are expected to take place: I-71/75 northbound off-ramp to 12th Street/MLK Jr. Blvd. (0.0 - 0.28 mile points): this closure will remain in place through Summer 2027. Detour: Traffic will use the I-71/75 northbound 5th Street exit ramp, turn left (north) onto Philadelphia Street, then left onto 4th Street driving west to the I-71/75 southbound ramp to Pike Street. Turn left on to Pike Street, then right on to Simon Kenton Way, then left on to MLK Blvd. KYTC will provide further updates ahead of the closures to inform all road users via the Brent Spence Bridge Corridor project website. [links-1.govdelivery.com] Project schedules are subject to change due to inclement weather or other unforeseen circumstances. item.title: 302172 : I-64 East-West between MM 53.0 and 58.0 Between U.S. 127 and U.S. 60 in Franklin County
item.description: Construction / Road Work : The Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) advises motorists of overnight alternating lane closures on Interstate 64 East and West beginning Friday, Aug. 21, in Franklin County. Overnight alternating lane closures will occur on I-64 East and West between mile markers 53 and 58 (between U.S. 127 and U.S. 60) during overnight hours from 7 p.m. to 6 a.m. each night beginning Friday, Aug. 21, through Friday, Aug. 28 (overnight work will not occur on the night of Saturday, Aug. 22). The overnight alternating lane closures are necessary for contract crews to install pavement markers and rumble strips along the corridor. Motorists are advised to follow all lane closure restrictions, use caution when traveling through work zone, and plan for additional travel time. The work is part of the I-64 improvement project between the Frankfort exits (mile markers 53 and 58), which includes milling and removing the existing asphalt surface, followed by resurfacing with new asphalt pavement. Other improvements to the 5-mile corridor include bridge repairs and bridge crash wall repairs. Construction is scheduled to be completed by the Fall of 2026.

item.title: 302276 : I-71 North Ramp to KY 1039 in Gallatin County
item.description: Construction / Road Work : The Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) advises motorists of an upcoming ramp closure on Interstate 71 northbound in Gallatin County beginning at 8 p.m. on Sunday, Aug. 23. Crews will close the I-71 northbound off-ramp to Exit 55 (KY 1039). During the closure, crews will perform ramp work, including milling and paving operations, ramp widening and shoulder work. Due to the scope of work, the ramp will be closed continuously for an extended period during this phase of the project. A signed detour will be in place utilizing I-71 northbound to Exit 57 (KY 35/Sparta Pike) to I-71 southbound to Exit 55 (KY 1039). Weather permitting, these ramp closures are expected to remain in place through Sunday, Sept. 6. Additional updates will be provided if more time is needed to complete the work. Additionally, a single lane closure on I-71 northbound between Exit 55 and Exit 57 will begin at 7 p.m. on Sunday, Aug. 23, to allow crews to adjust the barrier wall. The single lane closure is expected to be removed by 8 a.m. on Monday, Aug. 24. This work is being performed as part of the ongoing I-71 widening project on an approximately 4.59 mile portion of I-71 in Gallatin and Carroll counties. As the new ramp closure begins Sunday night, two ramps that have been closed since Sun., Aug. 9, will reopen: * Exit 55 (KY 1039) on-ramp to I-71 northbound * I-71 northbound off-ramp to Exit 57 (KY 35/Sparta Pike) Project Background A project aimed at reducing congestion and improving safety on a portion of I-71 in Gallatin and Carroll counties began on March 3, 2025. The project will widen I-71 from its configuration of two lanes in each direction, to three lanes in each direction with a shared median wall. I-71 is being widened in the following areas: Gallatin County: beginning at the Carroll/Gallatin County line (mile point 53.41) extending northeasterly to west of Sparta Pike (KY 35) (mile point 57.36), a distance of 3.95 miles. Carroll County: beginning at mile point 52.77 extending northeasterly to the Carroll/Gallatin County line (mile point 53.41), a distance of 0.64 miles. Traffic on I-71 northbound has been shifted from the original northbound lanes into the median while crews reconstruct the original northbound lanes. Two lanes of northbound traffic are being maintained and separated by the permanent barrier wall. During this phase, crews are removing the existing pavement and completing shoulder work on I-71 northbound. This widening project includes a bridge replacement over KY 47. The existing bridges are being replaced with a new, single-span bridge matching the median widening throughout the project area. The speed limit has been reduced throughout the project area to 55 miles-per-hour to keep crews safe as they work to improve the corridor. Eaton Asphalt Paving Co., Inc. is contracted to perform the nearly $42 million project on behalf of KYTC. Weather permitting, the overall project has an expected completion date of Nov. 1, 2026. You can find more information on the project here [links-1.govdelivery.com]. Project schedules are subject to change due to inclement weather or other unforeseen circumstances.
